draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kumarakom! It's a cluster of small islands on Vembanad, the largest lake in Kerala. The old Baker family house here is the 'History House' from Arundhati Roy's The God of Small Things.
draft.hungryLine: Karimeen pollichathu, pearl spot fish grilled in banana leaf over coal, is the dish here, and the little toddy shops at R-block do great seafood if your boat stops there.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Start at the bird sanctuary on the banks of Vembanad Lake, then look in at the Bay Island Driftwood Museum.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take a backwater boathouse ride. It's what Kumarakom is most loved for, and it works for a couple or a big group.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Four generations of the British Baker family lived here until 1962, speaking Malayalam and even wearing the mundu.

spots.detail: Malarikkal · Fields of pink water lilies

legends.title: Kari Saipu
legends.body: Locals called the missionary Alfred George Baker 'Kari Saipu', maybe a twist on 'Baker Sahib'. Arundhati Roy used the name in her novel too.

legends.title: Take the thickest piece
legends.body: There's a local saying: 'If thou are in the land of rat snake stew, thou shalt choose the thickest piece.' Some toddy shops still serve frog legs and crane fry if you're brave.

tips.title: See the lilies at dawn.
tips.body: The water lily farms bloom only in August and September, and the flowers wilt once the sun gets on them.

tips.title: Ask for a good chef on your boat.
tips.body: Boat rentals aren't cheap, so book with a reliable company and ask for a chef who knows the local food.

story.title: Kari Saipu's house
story.body: British missionary Alfred George Baker built a house here. His family would stay for four generations.

story.title: A school
story.body: One of the Baker daughters started the Baker Memorial School in Kottayam.

story.title: The Bakers leave
story.body: The last Bakers moved out, and the house slowly fell into ruin.

story.title: The God of Small Things
story.body: Arundhati Roy set her book in Ayemenem, right next door, and made the Baker house her 'History House'. The Taj group later restored it as a hotel, and the book's success brought more visitors.

story.title: In the news
story.body: The New York Times wrote about Kumarakom's backwater tourism.
